title: EventBus.localConsumer and EventBus.consumer interfer with each other

comments.body: what happens if you use send instead of publish ?

When using send, the second message is handled by only one of the handlers (either the localConsumer or the consumer), and the first message is still not handled at all. So the behaviour is basically the same, with the only exception, that at most one handler will be called.
But send() is not what we want here, we want to publish(), because we want all handlers to be called, only not the local consumers, if the message was published on a different cluster member.

Hi @npomaroli , this has been reported a few times in the past. It is a known limitation of the eventbus implementation.

Can you give some details about your use case? In particular, we'd like to understand why you want to have local and clustered consumers on the same node for the same address. Thanks

Hi @tsegismont,
we use vert.x in our headless CMS https://github.com/gentics/mesh.
If a CMS entity (which we call "node") is modified, e.g. by a call to the REST API, the instance handling the request publishes an event to the address "mesh.node.updated", so that any kind of consumers will be notified about the data change.

In a clustered environment, we want **all** CMS instances to handle this event by clearing their (local) caches, so the event handler for "clear cache when node is modified" is a eventbus.consumer().

Our CMS can also index the contents stored in the nodes in an (external) elasticsearch installation, and when a node is modified, we need to re-index it, but clearly, we only want **one** instance to do this, since all CMS instances are connected with the same elasticsearch cluster anyways, so the event handler for "re-index node if changed" is a event.localConsumer().

Note, that this is only an example, we use the eventbus for lot's of messages in our CMS and it is possible for our customers to write plugins, that might register consumers or local consumers for their own purposes.
Are there any updates on this?
Not yet, we have planned to look into it after 4.2.4 is out
